newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy trade union says open to some pension reform.
newsitem.headline: Italy trade union says open to some pension reform.

text.p: CISL, one of Italy's three big labour confederations, is willing to discuss a rebalance of social welfare spending and considers that some overhaul of the pensions system is possible, CISL leader Sergio D'Antoni said.

But he stressed in an opening address to the CISL annual congress that any such adjustment to social spending should not reduce the overall total of expenditure as a percentage of gross domestic product.
"As long as the GDP/social spending ratio is maintained then CISL is willing to discuss a different distribution and rebalance," D'Antoni said.
But he repeated that Italian trades unions were opposed to any changes to the pensions sistem being made until 1998.
"Perfect reforms do not exist, only socially and politically possible reforms. But some overhaul is possible," he said.

Cabinet secretary Enrico Micheli said on Tuesday that the country's creaking welfare state needed rebalancing but said that this should be achieved without cutting overall social spending as a percentage of gross domestic product.
D'Antoni urged Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government to put a halt to the continual outpouring of leaks and rumours about possible pension reforms.
"If you have a concrete proposal on social welfare reform then we are ready to discuss it. We don't have any taboos or obstinacy, we have arguments to put forward," he said.
"The root of the crisis in our welfare state is in the lack of jobs. We don't intend to just accept the idea of an inevitable decline, we need profound and urgent political measures," D'Antoni added.

Prodi's government has said it aims to reform the country's unwieldy and costly pensions system based on consultations with unions and employers, the results of which will be contained in the budget for 1998.
Broad outlines on planned reforms will be included in the government's three-year economic target programme (DPEF) expected to be presented next week.
